newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain regions angered by PP-Basque tax deal.
newsitem.headline: Spain regions angered by PP-Basque tax deal.

text.p: Spanish regional governments hit back on Friday at a government deal with the Basque government, which allowed the authority to collect special taxes on such items as alcohol, tobacco or petrol.
The regional governments of Castilla and Leon, Rioja, Asturias and Cantabria lodged official protests against the deal, Spanish National Radio said.

"The agreement with the Basque regional government may not and should not discriminate against the other regional governments. But the other 15 regions feel discriminated against this morning," opposition Socialist Party legislative spokesman Joaquin Almunia told Spanish National Radio.

The Basque region, which enjoys more extensive taxation rights than other regions for historic reasons, wrung out the right to collect special taxes in exchange for the group's five votes in favour of the minority government's 1997 budget draft.

Provisions for regional collection are included in an overall five-year package negotiated between the central government and the regions this week, but only the Basques may actually exercise the privilege for the time being.
Jordi Pujol, president of the government's key Catalan allies, said the deal was a foothold for his regional government's aspirations for greater taxation authority.
"This is good for the Basque government and also for us, because we had left this issue parked but from now on we will go back to it to make sure Catalunya also strives for it," Pujol told the radio.
Catalunya will strive for similar treatment in 2001, when the next general regional financing framework is negotiated.
